title: Invoice intake & approval routing
description: An n8n workflow that reads invoice PDFs from an accounts-payable inbox and routes each one to the ledger, a manager or a person for review. Built by Dyaksa.
intro: An n8n workflow that watches an accounts-payable inbox, reads each invoice PDF and routes it: to the ledger, to a manager for approval, or to a person when it can't be read. Scroll to follow one invoice through all 14 nodes.

stations.title: It starts in the inbox finance already uses.
stations.body: An IMAP trigger watches the accounts-payable mailbox, downloads attachments and marks each message read, so the same invoice isn't picked up twice.
check: Watch Invoices Inbox · INBOX, mark as read

stations.title: Replies and newsletters are ignored.
stations.body: The first attachment's MIME type has to contain pdf. A reply, a newsletter or an image ends at a No Operation node, and nothing is written anywhere.
check: Has PDF Attachment? · false → No Operation

stations.title: Readable rules pull out what someone used to type.
stations.body: Extract From File gets the PDF's text. A Code node finds the invoice number, total, due date and vendor with plain regex rules, and strips thousands separators so 1,240.50 compares as a number.
stations.code:
const amountMatch = text.match(/total\s*(?:due)?\s*[:\$]?\s*([0-9,]+\.\d{2})/i);
const amount = amountMatch ? parseFloat(amountMatch[1].replace(/,/g, '')) : null;
check: Extract PDF Text → Parse Invoice Fields

stations.title: If it can't read an invoice, it says so.
stations.body: An invoice counts as complete only when the number, amount and due date were all found. Anything less goes to a Needs Review sheet and #finance-ops hears about it. A half-filled row never reaches the ledger.
check: Fields Complete? · false → Needs Review → Slack

stations.title: The approval policy is one number.
stations.body: Amounts over 1,000 go to a manager. The threshold lives in one IF node, so changing the policy is a one-field edit finance can read. Anything under it is logged to the ledger as auto_approved.

stations.title: The manager gets the details, not a forwarded email.
stations.body: The invoice is appended to Pending Approval as awaiting_approval, then #finance-approval gets the number, vendor, amount and due date. Ledger, approval and review are separate sheets, so each queue can be worked and audited on its own.
check: Log To Approval Queue → Alert Finance Manager

stations.title: When the workflow itself fails, someone hears.
stations.body: An Error Trigger catches any failed execution, whether IMAP, Sheets or Slack broke, and posts the error message to #eng-alerts.

stations.title: 14 nodes, three queues.
stations.body: Every invoice ends in exactly one place: the ledger, the approval queue or the review queue. The regex parser is swappable on purpose: replace it with an LLM extractor and every node after it stays the same, because the JSON it hands on doesn't change.

edgeCases: Email with no PDF (reply, newsletter, image attachment)
